summary: Confirmed that LMCRadixCache dropped cache_salt on both MP lookup and store. The candidate forwards salt when LMCache advertises supports_cache_salt, fails closed for salted requests on older connectors, preserves unsalted compatibility, and makes MP store cleanup exception-safe.

tests.what_was_measured: Regression failed against the prepared base because lookup/store did not propagate cache_salt, legacy salted access was not gated, cleanup was not exception-safe, and the documented contract still excluded external storage.

Five focused contract and boundary tests passed: salted lookup forwarding, salted legacy fail-closed behavior, unsalted legacy compatibility, salted store handoff/gating, and exception-safe MP cleanup.
44 tests and 61 subtests passed, covering the focused LMCache boundary plus existing RadixKey/RadixCache behavior.
Changed Python files compiled and the patch had no whitespace errors.

remaining_limitations: No live MP daemon end-to-end reproduction was possible because LMCache is absent from the prepared environment and its companion salt-aware connector API is not yet released or merged.
No GPU execution was performed: this is cache-key metadata routing, and without the LMCache package/daemon a GPU run would not independently validate wire-key isolation.
The candidate is limited to LMCache MP mode. IP/XPU mode and extra_key/LoRA external namespacing remain outside this issue's coordinated fix.
Deployment must use an LMCache connector that advertises supports_cache_salt=True for salted external reuse; older connectors intentionally keep salted requests local.
